title: docs(components): the toggle-group schema block teaches `type` for the selection mode, but the renderer reads `selectionType`
body:
Measured while implementing #4632 (PR #4651). Filed unassigned. Duplicate-searched (keyword + the docs path): no open issue covers it.

Left deliberately unfixed in PR #4651: that card scoped to the `icon` / `disabled` keys on `ToggleGroupItem`, and this is a different key in the same block.

## The defect

`content/docs/components/disclosure/toggle-group.mdx` documents the component schema as:

```plaintext
interface ToggleGroupSchema {
  type: 'toggle-group';
  type: 'single' | 'multiple';    // Selection mode
  ...
}
```

Two problems in two lines:

1. **`type` is declared twice** in one interface block — not valid TypeScript, so the block cannot be what it presents itself as.
2. **The selection-mode key does not exist.** `ToggleGroupSchema` in `packages/types/src/disclosure.ts` declares `selectionType?: 'single' | 'multiple'`, and `packages/components/src/renderers/disclosure/toggle-group.tsx` reads `schema.selectionType` (defaulting to `'single'`). An author following this page writes `type: 'single'`, which either collides with the component discriminator or is simply dropped — and the group silently stays single-select.

The catalog entries next to it get this right (all three author `selectionType`), so the docs page is the only surface teaching the wrong spelling.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a drive-by

Same reasoning as #4632, which this was found next to: the docs are part of the corpus AI authoring tools retrieve from, and here the corpus does not merely teach a dead key — it teaches a key whose declared meaning belongs to the type discriminator. That is the "declared = enforced" property inverted at the authoring end.

The fix is small (rename the line to `selectionType?: 'single' | 'multiple'` and drop the duplicate), but it should be taken with a check of whether other component pages in `content/docs/components/**` carry the same hand-written-block drift — that sweep is the actual value of the card.

Refs #4632, PR #4651.
